title: Thrombophilia tests: validity by timing and anticoagulant
scopeNote: Whether each result can be trusted during acute thrombosis or on UFH/LMWH, a VKA or a DOAC. Inherited thrombophilia testing rarely changes default antiplatelet therapy after arterial stroke unless it shows APS or venous thrombosis (Kleindorfer 2021). AT, protein C and protein S deficiency can be acquired, and levels vary within a person (Middeldorp 2023). "Not addressed by sources" means no source in this app covers that cell.

notes.text: Pre-analytic: levels rise about 15–20% per hour in unseparated blood at room temperature — keep on ice or separate promptly.

notes.text: Raised by renal impairment, B12/folate deficiency, methotrexate, nitrous oxide and anticonvulsants.

pitfalls: Sending the full panel during the acute admission — AT, protein C/S and LA are least reliable then; genotypes and solid-phase aPL are not affected (Stevens 2016; Devreese 2020)
Treating an abnormal APCR on a DOAC or warfarin as factor V Leiden — send PCR (Favaloro 2019)
Leaving the anticoagulant off the LA request (Devreese 2020)
keyNumbers: LA on LMWH: draw ≥12 h after the dose, with anti-Xa (Devreese 2020)
LA on a DOAC: hold ≥48 h if feasible (longer with renal impairment) and check a DOAC level (Devreese 2020)
Homocysteine after stroke: recheck at ≥3 months if it changes management (Meiklejohn 2001; Haapaniemi 2007; Shi 2018)
